In just under 30 hours, I completed the game and the majority of all important sidequests. While I did enjoy my time in the Andromeda Galaxy, and was deeply immersed for the first good chunk of the game, that immersion unfortunately met a rather fateful end as I found myself running back and forth between every location in the galaxy, time and time again, for exceptionally medial tasks. Either as some kind of poetic design, or in an effort to increase the average user's game time, Andromeda has been designed around a system that really, really loves repetitive tasks. "Do this three times, go there three times," etc, etc. Additionally, the variety in the form of enemy types and capabilities was quite lackluster. For the most part, you only really fight four or five different categories of enemy in the entire game.

I have heard the multiplayer is great; but I never got the opportunity to play it. So, this section remains unfilled for now as far as this review goes.

The Tempest Crew is fun, but they don't really stack up to the Normandy's in the way of genuine companionship. I was disappointed when I discovered that I couldn't in any way customize my squad's loadouts or appearances; rendering the game more simple and accessible, but lackluster in the same area. In some cases, the more interesting parts of the story are just the teasers for DLC that will never be released. The open world exploration available to you on most planets is actually quite impressive; but you will find no shortage of awkward if not outright annoying issues with the terrain if you try to stray too far off of the designed path. (This is more noticeable on some planets than others.)

Overall I did think the gunplay and movement was a significant improvement over the original trilogy; for the most part I would be delighted to see the combat system return for future titles. It was very nice to be able to sprint, dodge, and double jump with the use of your jump pack, giving you far more freedom of movement than afforded to Commander Shepard in their games.

Finally, when it comes to the immersion; there is nothing short of beauty to be found in this game, once you have fine tuned the settings to properly suit your graphics card and system. The Tempest is a very iconic ship, and the observation windows allowing you to actually see your location in the galaxy is a great touch. The sound design is top tier, and most of the planets are great. Unfortunately, this praise is not entirely universal as, especially in the case of interior locations, designs become very repetitive and dull. Sometimes this adds to immersion, when it comes to the industrialized, streamlined vessels. Other times its just irritating. Andromeda is one of those games that will have you wondering "Just what were these aliens thinking when they designed this structure?!"

If you've already had your fill of the main Mass Effect trilogy and want more, then yes, play Andromeda. But if you're on the hunt for your very first introduction to the franchise; this isn't it.

This game got pretty bad reviews at launch, i think partly because of (misguided) expectations. There are still a few minor animation bugs left, but if you've enjoyed the previous games in the series, there's really no reason not to play this. Yes, it's not a direct sequel to the previous games and it tells a new story, but it's a solid game on it's own.
